title: the pipeline of the diagrams finds the instrument and draws both themes
intent: The wave that carries out the first piece of the catch-up plan (the track D, the wave D0): the site of Yeah is a static site, and the diagrams of the architecture were a drawing that nobody could redraw -- there was no script that turned a source of a diagram into a picture, so a change of the machine of the states changed nothing on the site and the picture rotted in silence.  The wave gives the site that script and the two skins of the themes.  (1) `scripts/dev diagrams` renders every diagram of `site/diagrams/` into `site/assets/diagrams/`, two pictures per diagram -- the light one and the dark one.  (2) The instrument is found by the script itself and not by the person: the chain of the search lives in one place, `scripts/lib/tools.sh`, the function `find_tool`, and it is the same chain for every tool -- the variable of the environment, the command on PATH, the binary of the user in `~/.nix-profile/bin`, and the store of nix when the caller names the glob.  The script answers with the code 3 when the instrument is not there, so 'the tool is not installed' is never read as 'the diagram is fine'.  (3) The skin of a theme is a file of its own, `site/diagrams/palette-light.puml` and `site/diagrams/palette-dark.puml`, and the colours of the skins are the tokens of the site -- `--face-default-bg`, `--face-default-fg`, `--face-fringe-bg`, `--face-divider`, `--face-prose` of `site/styles.css`.  (4) The file of a diagram keeps being a file of a diagram: the skin of a theme goes inside `@startuml`, so the sources stay readable and independent of each other.  The wave does not draw a single diagram: the first diagram (the machine of the states, born out of the code) is the wave D1, the other seven are the wave D2.  The wave also closes the finding of the catch-up plan about the chain of the search -- the plan said 'describe the real chain or add a step', and the wave did both at once.
objection: The claim is about a pipeline and not about a picture: the wave draws no diagram of the site, and the check draws a probe diagram (a state and a move) in a temporary tree, so the tree of the repository is never written.  What the check proves is that the pipeline works and that the two skins carry the colours of the site; what it cannot prove is that a diagram of the architecture is a good diagram -- that is the eye of the author and not a check.  The colours of the palettes are bound to the tokens of `site/styles.css` by name, so a rename of a token in the CSS breaks the check: that is the price of the binding and the point of it -- a palette that drifts from the site is a picture of another site.  The chain of the search ends in the store of nix, and the store is host-specific: the last step is the one that can differ from machine to machine, and the first match of the shell is taken, so the choice is the same on every run of the machine.  The step in the store is given to PlantUML only: in the store there are many versions of Emacs and the version of Emacs must not be a random choice, so `find_emacs` stops after three steps.  The pipeline is the instrument of the author and not a build step of the site: the published site carries the ready SVG, and a site that has no PlantUML is not broken -- it is a site whose pictures were drawn earlier.  The code 3 of the missing instrument is the code of 'unknown', and it is the same code the checks of the method use for a machine that cannot answer.
refuted_by: a diagram of the site is not rendered in both themes, or the pipeline renders one theme only, or the pipeline does not find PlantUML by itself, or the pipeline answers with the code 0 when the tool is not there, or the skins of the themes do not carry the colours of the site, or the control of the claim does not make the check fail by its own assertion
note: The claim of the wave is new: `the-diagram-pipeline-renders-both-themes`.  Seven controls were applied to copies of the tree on 2026-11-20, and every one of them ended with the verdict the control asked for.  (1) One theme only (the control of the claim): the loop of the themes loses the dark one -- the check says that the pipeline did not report two pictures, that the dark picture is missing, and that the tree of the pictures kept something that is not a picture of the probe; code 1.  (2) The chain of the search cannot find the instrument at all (the name on the PATH and the glob in the store are both wrong) -- the pipeline answers 3 where the two themes must be drawn; code 1.  (3) The code 3 of the missing instrument became the code 0 -- the check says that the pipeline answered 0 where PlantUML is not there and the answer must be 3; code 1.  (4) The dark skin is gone -- the verdict is 1 (a broken promise) and not 2 (a machine that cannot answer); this control is what forced the early exit of the check.  (5) A colour of the palette is not a token of the site (`StateBorderColor #123456') -- the check says that the property of the skin and the token of the site differ, and that the palette carries a colour the site does not know; code 1.  (6) The background of the palette drifts from the token of the site (`#FEFEFE' instead of `#ffffff') -- the check says the same and the picture of the probe does not carry the background of the site; code 1.  (7) The words of the report of the pipeline change -- the check still answers 0: a check that leans on a wording is a check that fails on a spelling.  The measurement of the wave: each of the two palettes carries 23 lines of `skinparam' and five distinct colours, and every colour of both palettes is a colour of `site/styles.css'; the check is 13.6 kB and goes in 2.6 seconds; the whole set of the checks of the method and the unit tests are green.  The full set of the checks found one real mismatch of its own: the documents named `site/assets/diagrams/', and that directory was not in the repository -- the path of the pictures led nowhere, and the check `the-documentation-points-at-files-that-exist' said so in five lines of four documents.  The wave created the directory (`site/assets/diagrams/.gitkeep' -- git keeps no empty directory) and told it in the documents: the path of the pictures is a path of the repository, and the pictures themselves arrive with the waves D1 and D2.
